_note: Physics parameters (spec 7.10). 'values' is what the physics loads; 'docs' gives each value's unit, source and note. Change a value only with its source.

ball_mass_kg.note: Confirm against published 52.5 mm phenolic snooker ball sets (tuner, M1 wave 2).

slide_friction.source: spec 7.10; Alciatore, billiards.colostate.edu FAQ physical properties; pooltool (Apache-2.0) BallParams.u_s
slide_friction.note: Ball-cloth sliding friction. Sets how long stun and screw last before the ball grips.

roll_friction.source: spec 7.10 range 0.005-0.01 for fast snooker cloth
roll_friction.note: Rolling resistance; calibrated against C11 (table speed) by the tuner.

spin_friction_per_r.note: Spinning friction divided by R; side spin decays at 5/2 * this * g rad/s^2.

ball_restitution.note: Tuned against C2/C3 (stun stop and follow-through).

ball_friction_a.source: Alciatore, billiards.colostate.edu TP A-14 fit; pooltool (Apache-2.0) AlciatoreBallBallFriction.a
ball_friction_a.note: Ball-ball friction mu = a + b exp(-c v_rel), v_rel in m/s. Gives throw and spin transfer (C6).

ball_friction_b.source: Alciatore, billiards.colostate.edu TP A-14 fit; pooltool (Apache-2.0) AlciatoreBallBallFriction.b

ball_friction_c.source: Alciatore, billiards.colostate.edu TP A-14 fit; pooltool (Apache-2.0) AlciatoreBallBallFriction.c

cushion_restitution.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873, snooker values (cushion agent confirms)
cushion_restitution.note: e_e in the Mathavan model; with the friction terms it gives the speed-dependent loss (C7).

cushion_friction.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873 mu_w (cushion agent confirms)

cushion_table_friction.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873 mu_s (cushion agent confirms)
cushion_table_friction.note: Ball-cloth friction during the cushion impact.

cushion_contact_height_m.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873: h = 7R/5 (sin theta = 2/5)
cushion_contact_height_m.note: Sets theta = asin((h - R) / R), the angle of the cushion's push; running and check side depend on it (C8).

cushion_rigid_limit_m_s.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873, Fig. 7: the model holds up to 2.5 m/s normal speed
cushion_rigid_limit_m_s.note: Above it the cushion stops acting rigid; restitution falls by cushion_restitution_slope_per_m_s.

cushion_restitution_slope_per_m_s.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873, Fig. 7 (fitted by the cushions agent / tuner)
cushion_restitution_slope_per_m_s.note: 0 is the pure model; a positive slope makes firm cushion and jaw hits lose more.

jaw_restitution.source: starting guess; spec 6.3 owner check (tight pockets)
jaw_restitution.note: Jaws use the cushion model with their own restitution: firm balls rattle, slow ones drop.

cue_mass_kg.note: Effective cue mass in the tip impulse.

cue_tip_restitution.source: starting guess within Marlow's / Alciatore, billiards.colostate.edu's tip efficiency range (cue agent confirms)
cue_tip_restitution.note: Sets how much cue speed becomes ball speed.

cue_end_mass_kg.source: pooltool (Apache-2.0) stick_ball/squirt.py model; tuned to C9 (1-3 degrees at maximum side)

miscue_speed_factor.note: A miscued ball keeps at most this fraction of the full-hit speed.

miscue_max_angle_rad.note: A miscue sends the ball within this angle of the aim.

cue_clearance_m.note: Margin the cue keeps over a rail or ball when the elevation is raised.

max_cue_speed_m_s.source: starting guess: above the hardest snooker shots

nap_tick_ratio.note: A rolling ball's nap is re-evaluated each time its speed falls by this factor.

nap_lateral_coeff.source: starting guess: about 1-2 cm of drift over a slow 1 m roll
nap_lateral_coeff.note: Spec 7.8: the owner's feel decides it.

nap_spin_coeff.note: Side spin holding with the nap; spec 7.8.

nap_speed_ref_m_s.note: Speed at which the lateral term equals nap_lateral_coeff * g.

time_cap_s.note: A shot still moving after this is stopped and logged (C12).

zero_time_s.note: Events closer than this are simultaneous.

max_zero_time_chain.note: Simultaneous events in a row before the guard trips (spec 7.7).
